newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metal futures mixed, gold firmer.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metal futures mixed, gold firmer.

text.p: Tokyo gold futures ended firmer across the board on Friday but off early highs as the yen's rebound against the dollar pared some of their gains, traders said.
Platinum and palladium futures ended mixed, slipping ahead of the close on fresh selling by private investors, they said.
Gold futures ranged from five yen to seven yen per gram firmer, with most-active benchmark February up seven yen at 1,380 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $351.10/40 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $351.30/80 in New York on Thursday.
In the gold futures market, private investors were liquidating long positions for most of the day, while trade houses bought futures and sold spot gold in arbitrage dealings.

Activity in the bullion market was lacklustre. "Good physical demand below $350 in Asia may prevent gold from falling sharply from current levels, but the market lacked bullish factors to push up gold sharply," one trader said.

"As a result, gold is likely to be sandwiched between $350 and $355 per ounce for the near term," he said, adding the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee (FOMC) next week may provide direction to the market.

In platinum and palladium futures, the focus was still on the prolonged delay in the resumption of Russian exports to Japan, the traders said. "Near-term direction is uncertain. Traders were wary of taking fresh positions, waiting for new information from Russia," one trader said.
In palladium futures, private investors were tending to build fresh short positions after covering shorts on Wednesday.
Benchmark February palladium was down four yen at 563 yen.
Benchmark February platinum was down seven yen at 1,463 yen. Benchmark February silver was up 1.0 yen per 10 grams at 206.0 yen. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk, +81-3-3432-7431
